{{Orphan|date=August 2025}}

A '''sum-check protocol''' is a [[cryptographic protocol]] for the construction of [[interactive proof system]]s,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Lund |first1=Carsten |last2=Fortnow |first2=Lance |last3=Karloff |first3=Howard |last4=Nisan |first4=Noam |date=1992-10-01 |title=Algebraic methods for interactive proof systems |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/146585.146605 |journal=Journal of the ACM |language=en |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=859–868 |doi=10.1145/146585.146605 |issn=0004-5411}}</ref> used widely in [[Zero-knowledge proof|zero-knowledge protocols]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=The intuition behind the sum-check protocol in 5 minutes - cryptologie.net |url=https://cryptologie.net/posts/the-intuition-behind-the-sum-check-protocol-in-5-minutes/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=cryptologie.net}}</ref>

== History ==
The sum-check protocol was created by [[Carsten Lund]], [[Lance Fortnow]], [[Howard Karloff]], and [[Noam Nisan]] and formalized in 1990.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Lund |first1=C. |last2=Fortnow |first2=L. |last3=Karloff |first3=H. |last4=Nisan |first4=N. |chapter=Algebraic methods for interactive proof systems |date=1990-10-01 |title=Proceedings &#91;1990&#93; 31st Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science |pages=2–10 vol.1 |doi=10.1109/FSCS.1990.89518 |isbn=0-8186-2082-X }}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Concept ==
In an [[Interactive proof system|interactive proof]], the goal is for a verifier V to offload an expensive computation to an untrusted prover P.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Thaler |first=Justin |date=2020-03-16 |title=The Unreasonable Power of the Sum-CheckProtocol |url=https://zkproof.org/2020/03/16/sum-checkprotocol/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=ZKProof Standards |language=en-US}}</ref> The sum-check protocol allows the prover to convince the verifier that the sum of a [[multivariate polynomial]] is equal to a known value.<ref name=":1" /> The goals of the sum-check protocol are to make the verifier run in time linear to the input size, to keep the proof logarithmically small, and to keep the prover efficient.<ref name=":2" />

For a ''v''-variate polynomial ''g'' defined over a finite field <math>\mathbb{F}</math>, the prover provides the verifier with the following sum:<ref>{{Cite book |last=Thaler |first=Justin |url=https://people.cs.georgetown.edu/jthaler/ProofsArgsAndZK.pdf |title=Proofs, Arguments, and Zero-Knowledge |date=July 18, 2023 |publisher=Georgetown University |pages=33 |language=en |chapter=3.1, 4.1, 4.2}}</ref>

<math>H := \sum_{b_1 \in \{0,1\}} \sum_{b_2 \in \{0,1\}} \cdots \sum_{b_v \in \{0,1\}} g(b_1, \ldots, b_v).</math>

Without a prover, the verifier has to perform <math>2^{n}</math> evaluations of ''g'' to verify the statement, which is a very large runtime. With the sumcheck protocol, the verifier's runtime is<math>O(v + \text{[the cost to evaluate } g \text{ at a single input in } \mathbf{F}^v ])</math>.<ref name=":2" />

== Limitations ==

=== Proof size ===
The sum-check protocol leads to proofs that are of at least logarithmic length.<ref name=":2" />

=== Zero-knowledge and succinctness ===
The protocol is not [[zero-knowledge proof|zero-knowledge]] by itself, and like all interactive proofs, it is not succinct for NP statements.<ref name=":2" />

[[zk-SNARK]] proofs combine the sum-check protocol with [[commitment scheme]]s to obtain zero-knwoledge and succinct arguments.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Citation |last1=Bagad |first1=Suyash |title=The Sum-Check Protocol over Fields of Small Characteristic |date=2024 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1046 |access-date=2025-08-25 |id=2024/1046 |last2=Domb |first2=Yuval |last3=Thaler |first3=Justin}}</ref>
